key_insight: Subquadratic attention changes the performance trade-offs of LLM inference, so disaggregation should be redesigned around its lower arithmetic intensity and smaller memory footprint. The paper shows this can unlock better throughput and energy efficiency than dense-attention-oriented serving systems.
problem_solved: Existing disaggregated serving systems are optimized for dense attention, which does not match the compute/memory characteristics of modern LLMs that use subquadratic attention. This mismatch can leave throughput and energy efficiency on the table.
method: Analyzes the arithmetic intensity and memory behavior of subquadratic-attention LLM inference.
Rethinks heterogeneous system disaggregation decisions to match these new workload characteristics.
Evaluates serving on emerging DRAM-based and SRAM-based hardware configurations to identify efficiency gains.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that model architecture changes should drive systems design choices, not just model scaling. It can reduce inference cost, improve throughput, and make frontier LLM serving more energy efficient.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison diagram: dense-attention disaggregation vs subquadratic-aware disaggregation

Pipeline graphic of heterogeneous inference stages across DRAM and SRAM components
Energy/throughput bar chart highlighting performance gains
paper_title: Rethinking Heterogeneous System Disaggregation for Subquadratic Attention
paper_authors: Arya Tschand, Yaosheng Fu, Vikram Sharma Mailthody, Nicolai Oswald, Po-An Tsai
